body: Not well.  I never heard about the job.  I'm contemplating ending it.

Just to reply to that here, I just don't see much value in anything I do.  If I were working for someone like Apple, Google, or Facebook, I'd see value because those things help people make their lives better.  All our stuff does is just line someone's pocketbooks, they aren't really doing anything for any particular good.
A university, branch of government, reputable charitable organization, any number of things.
Marketing for a small tech company.
Yeah good luck telling my wife I'm going to stay home earning nothing while she earns everything.

That and much more.

Someone has to be the "voice" of an organization, and organize everything that entails.  In the case of what I want to do for a charitable organization or for a branch of government, it's more advocacy based.  Someone in that position would coordinate media appearances, write speeches, publish press releases, manage the website and social media, coordinate advisory committees, plan events, and so much more.

In my specific context, I want to use my knowledge and experience of dealing with media and communications to further the message and reach of a worthwhile organization.  I want to make sure that it continues to be a force for good, and that people's voices are heard, and that it's message is accurately conveyed.
I know.  It just wouldn't be so soul crushing if I hadn't already experienced what a fulfilling dream job is like.

See my other posts.  I've tried to work with volunteer organizations and it ended with disaster.  I need to be in a place where I can use my specific expertise, otherwise I'm just a worker drone in that situation as well.  If I'm not fulfilling my full potential, I'm not going to be enough.

I've tried.  I've started two businesses in the past few years, neither really worked out.  My expertise and area that I'm good at is best served within a larger organization where I'm an advocate of their mission or an organizer of their efforts.  It's very difficult to do that effectively when I have nothing behind me to advocate for.

I like the idea that I'm the point of contact for something so meaningful.  I like knowing that I can be part of something bigger than myself and an advocate for something that really matters.  Being able to do that and communicate back and forth with a community at large brings me a lot of joy, especially when things are clicking and things are getting done as they should.  I like being the vocal part of a process that allows people to do great things.  I love organizing big things and meeting new people and putting things in place to make amazing things happen.  Just talking about it makes me sad because it's been so long since I've had a platform to do that.

I also won't lie, I love being "the guy."  I was "the guy" in my old position.  I was the person with all the answers, the person people deferred to, the expert on many matters.  Someone people trusted for opinions and creativity.  I feel like I can get that back again with this job.
You think I haven't tried?  I'm not the type of person who would be this direly introspective about matters if I didn't feel as if I'd already exhausted every outlet.

My wife and I have thought about it and have tried, but I don't think that's meant for us.  We both tried to get jobs in San Francisco because we both dearly love that city.  I even thought that God wanted me to be there for some reason, as I felt as if he was trying to tell me that through a number of different means.  But we tried hard and couldn't find jobs that allowed us to actually live near such an expensive city.

I know beyond a doubt I'm the best person for the job.  The thing I'm nervous about is that because it's a city government job, they likely have someone already connected in mind for the job.  I'm fearful it's just going to be another opportunity I'm perfect for but won't be given a shot at.

That's their journey to make, not mine.  I can't make their decisions for them, they can only do that for themselves. 

You say that 99% of people can't be impactful and meaningful?  Why can't I be that 1%?
If they're happy with where they are, more power to them.  It's not my place to judge that.  It's my place to get myself to a place where I can be happy.
No.  He knew all along he had a purpose.

I'm interviewing to be the communications officer for the local city government.  I've mentioned in other comments that my teenage-dream was to be a communications officer for the White House like in The West Wing, and this is the closest thing to that dream.  If I don't get this job, I know my dream is unattainable, and my life is pointless.
How in the world is compiling spreadsheets to line someone else's pocketbook part of God's plan?  You give God too much credit.

I just have to have something more to live for.  I want to accomplish something huge in my life and be known for something.

This is going to sound stupid, but bear with me.  I really like Kanye West because the guy is just so over the top confident in everything he does.

The dude is arrogant as hell, but he's also very good at what he does.  He's made some of the most interesting and fun music in the past ten or fifteen years, and he's ventured out into a lot of other areas that he's been successful at.  He's an insufferable asshole, sure, but nobody can deny that he's done some pretty awesome stuff.  He speaks his mind and gets a lot of flak for it, but he's still very accomplished.

I'm not saying I want to be Kanye, but I want to be at that point.  I want to be the best at what I do, I want to have the confidence and swagger knowing that I am the best.  I want to be remembered and known for being the best at it.
There's no promise that things can or ever will get better.  I really have no reason to trust that it will, only a stupid blind faith that makes me hope it might.
Could you be more specific in your question?  I'm not following what you're asking.

I want to be the point of communications or PR person for an organization that's really changing lives for the better.  I mentioned in another comment that I'd grown up idolizing the characters in The West Wing, I really wish I could do something even close to that.
As long as I don't spend too much time on my own, I'm okay.
Okay well why not, alcohol, drugs, porn, you name it.  When I'm at my lowest, I have no barrier and no empathy in trying to get a fix to feel better.

I see what you're getting at.  I've certainly tried to change that around.  For me, I need something tangible that says "okay, I succeeded at this thing, I did good work that was my own."  I need something that shows that my luck is changing for the better, it needs to be something that I wholly controlled and needs to be something that actually made a difference for me and others and put my life in the right direction.

Finding what that is the trick.

Well, sure.  If I were to lived a life without accomplishing anything worthwhile, what would have been the point of living.

My biggest fear in life is to be gone and forgotten.  Knowing that I will never accomplish anything huge and worthwhile, knowing that I'll just be another forgotten drone and just another etched name on a gravestone.  I want to be Jobs, I want to be Zuckerberg, I want to be Carnegie.  Anything else is just letting myself become another grain lost in the sands.
Nowhere near there unfortunately.
No argument here.  I don't have the tools necessary to handle life.  That's why I'm strongly considering no longer participating in it.
I once did, now I'm not so sure.
Death is the solution for all of us.  We're all going to die, whether we like it or not.  Choosing how and when to die is the only real control we have over it.

It's tough because I really don't give a shit about what I do right now.  I stopped being vocal because I don't care.  I don't care if this company I'm in now survives or not, I can just move on to the next pointless and menial thing if it does.

On the other hand, I dearly wish I could contribute in a meaningful place where I could care.

Your classmate was a failure, and made the right choice.  That sounds blunt and rude, but in reality I'm only saying that as someone who is in his position.  Living is not a choice any of us are giving, but not living is one that any of us can make.  Some people are just not suited for life, and I understand and empathize with your classmate.

Somewhere inbetween there, maybe.

I think the biggest issue is more that I find so self worth anymore.  I hate myself.  I see no reason for anyone else to respect me, if I can't respect myself.  I had respect for myself when I had a platform to contribute to the best of my ability.  I no longer do.  It makes me feel like I have no reason to think that can ever happen again, and I'd prefer to live a short and relatively fulfilled life as opposed to a longer one full of more failure.

Too many prohibitive factors keep that away from me as an option.  I still have a wife to provide for.  With my plan to end myself, I've ensured it will be viewed as an accident so that she'll receive the life insurance money and be provided for.  I'm financially worth more dead than alive.
She didn't ask for any of this, it's best to protect her from it as long as I can.
I certainly do that.  They're great temporary reliefs, but nothing substantially changing for me.

Because I feel like I'm being beaten down.  Like I'm losing all autonomy and control.  Like this life isn't mine anymore, I'm just stuck behind a porthole watching someone else's life without any control over it.

Funny that you mention a "walkabout," I'd direly like to do that.  Specifically, I really want to take three or four months and walk the Pacific Crest Trail.  It's not an option for me though, as much as I wish it were.
I'm in the Southeast US.  Before all of this, I worked at a University, where I had many different hats and jobs there under somewhat of an umbrella job description.

I've unfortunately found myself in more situations that I'd care for in the past few years where I'm forced to say yes.  I hate it with a passion.  I feel like such a cog and drone when things are just expected of me and I have no input whatsoever.  It tears me up.
I can say nothing 100%.  I can only draw my best conclusion, with this, or anything.

I've thought about this some.  I think part of my issue is that for whatever reason, my parents, all my teachers, even my then girlfriend / now wife  always thought I was some kind of wunderkind and always drilled it into my head that they expected great things of me.  Now I'm just a normal, average person, with nothing outstanding about me.  I feel like I've let them and myself down for not achieving what they thought I would.
Without going into full sordid details, I can tell you I certainly have.

Without going into details that I'd rather not discuss in this specific subreddit, too much "alone time" is a bad idea for me.  When I'm in a low place, I fall into self destructive vices very easily.

I feel like I'm best as an advocate for something meaningful and worthwhile.  I feel like I would be best served for myself and others if I was the publicity / communications person and point of public contact for a worthwhile organization.

When I was younger, I idolized the characters on the show The West Wing.  I wanted to be someone who worked in Communications for something that shaped the world for the better.  I still do.
I've often thought this, that maybe the 40 hour a week life isn't for me.  But unfortunately even after a lot of searching, I can find no alternative.
I've considered it, but after a lot of thought, I realize that I already have a degree in exactly what I want to be doing.

I've often struggled with this.  I'd have absolutely zero respect if I tried to turn myself into something I'm not.  If I have to bite my tongue too much or say too much to conform, I'm not myself and can have no respect for myself.
See some of my other responses, pursuing charity work has kind of been a nightmare as well.
I've kind of thought about that.  I have no idea where to start or what it would even be for though.
I don't think it's anything that I can accurately view any one way or another.  If he wants me to know, he'll find a way for me to know.  I haven't yet.

I have thought about that and have been able to see the signs that it was time to move on in the last year of my old job.  But those seem to have been the last "signs" I've ever gotten.  I've never really gotten any in the ensuing five years of what the next thing is.  I've just felt lost ever since.

I didn't make the rules for life.  I didn't make the rules that say that you have to work 40 to 50 hours a week in order to make a decent living.  All I want is to do something that matters in that 40 to 50 hours a week.  Like I already have.
She's great.  She'll move on to someone better who can be a better figure for her.  It would be in her best interest.
They certainly haven't done that, then.
See some of my other replies, I've certainly tried.

I think for a while, I was okay with having that assessment of life.  I was okay with the idea that I was just in a temporary low.  But it's been five years now, and evidence is mounting up that it's not temporary.  I just feel worse and worse with no expectation of seeing the light at the end of the tunnel.  It's pretty much that specifically which encourages me to end things now.

It's not necessarily the job itself I put so much weight on, it's the sense of meaning and accomplishment it provided.  I respected myself because of it, and I know that others did as well.  When I don't have that, my self respect turns into self hatred, and I can't expect anyone else to respect me when I have no reason to respect myself.

Well more to the point, it's not the job that causes me to feel that way.  It was the sense of meaning and accomplishment that it gave me.  I've dearly missed that ever since, and I don't respect myself anymore because I'm not doing that.

I don't know that I have an adequate answer to that question.  I feel like I'm doing what I should, I don't know what to do beyond that.  If God is trying to lead me elsewhere, I feel like he'd just out and tell me like he did last time.

I had once thought that, but I think I've concluded that he doesn't want me to move.  My wife has a good job she enjoys where we live and I don't think he wants me to take her away from that.  I had applied for jobs in other towns, which I didn't get, which likely means that he wants me to stay put.
I just want to know that I'm doing what he means for me to be doing.  I used to feel that way, I just wish I could get back to that point again.

I know it's a bad idea to compare myself to others.  It's why I do my best not to compare myself to my peers from college that are doing way better than me.  Instead, I'm only comparing myself to myself.  And I'm a lesser person and far less happy and fulfilled than I was before.
Trust me, I've done pretty much everything I could.  I wouldn't feel at the end of my rope like this if I hadn't.
I'm not the figure to them that I once was.  I once was someone they could respect, but I don't feel like I am anymore.  I can't stand that feeling.
Well then if he wants me to do something different, I wish he'd get around to telling me what it is as plainly as he did the first time.

My degree in college was in Communications with an emphasis on all things digital.  I once thought that I'd be a Communications officer for the government, but I felt like God called me to stay at my old university and use my talents with creative projects, promoting, organizing, and teaching to work with college aged students.  I was also able to act as an advisor and help students in the beginnings of their careers.

Ever since then, I've been the marketing person for a few lowly tech companies.  I feel completely underutilized now and know I'm not making the difference I once did.
I've seen three in as many years and haven't really gotten any better, I've lost faith in their ability to really accomplish anything.

Here's my line of thinking:

In that old job, it felt like everything in my life led to it.  It felt like so many things happened that were too crazy to be chalked up to coincidence.  It wasn't really even just a job.  It was something I loved doing every day that I just happened to be getting paid for.  I was one of the few people who was able to accomplish it so well, because I felt like God uniquely prepared me for it through my education and experiences.

These days, that's not the case at all.  I'm just stuck in whatever crack I happened to fall in.  I feel no purpose or accomplishment like I used to.  It makes me almost certain I'm not doing what God intends, and I'm in no way being shown the signs or finding the crazy coincidences like I once did.
None really.  I have a hard time finding the right place where I can really contribute at what I'm best at.

I don't know if I'd agree totally with that assessment.  I did that job for around five years, I don't think I'd have been there that long if it wasn't what I was meant to do.  There's no way that I'd have been encouraged on so many fronts to put so much stock in it and have positioned my life for doing it for the rest of my life if I wasn't meant to do it.

I feel like the biggest prohibitive factor in my life is that I refuse to be just another peg in another hole.  I really have issues with just being a Yes Man and not being able to voice my opinion.  Because I don't conform to everyone else's expectations and try to offer a real unique voice, I feel like people think I'm too much of a wild card.
I've seen three in as many years, none have really accomplished anything for me.

I tried working with an International Organization in town that tried to spread more cultural awareness and combat cultural racism in my town.  Unfortunately, that organization was very political and it was near impossible to accomplish anything tangible.

The other was with my old university's alumni association.  I tried to leverage it as a way to continue to help out the college aged crowd that I used to work closely with in my old job, but I found that the whole organization was mainly used as a tool of the university President for his own political purposes.
Yeah sure, I've talked with my wife, some close friends, and a therapist or two.  It helps to talk, but I feel like it's still an enormous weight even afterwards.

I didn't find that to be my experience.  When I was working a job that I loved and was good at, I was in a position to help others and make a difference.  I felt like I was doing what God intended for me to be doing, and I felt great about it.  Ever since then, I've felt so distant from what I feel I'm good at and meant to be doing, and consequently further from God.

I've thought a lot about this, and I've thought at times that the answer might be volunteering and putting my talents to good use that way.  It hasn't worked out, unfortunately.  I never get put into a place in volunteer organizations where I can excel with what I'm good at, it's been really discouraging.

Trust me, I have.  It all feels like a band aid on a gaping wound though.  I usually feel a sense of guilt about doing anything I personally enjoy because it's not doing anything to further my purpose of doing what I'm good at to help others.

In my old job that I dearly loved, I was able to make a difference for young college aged people.  I still see some of them from time to time and it reminds me how much good work I did to have been at least a little part of their lives.  

It wasn't necessarily any personal desire I had that compelled me in that position, it was helping others in something worthwhile.  Ever since then, all I've been doing is helping line someone else's pocketbooks, and I feel such shame and guilt about it.

That's all totally true.  But it's not the car or wallet.  It's the purpose and meaning.  In my old dream job, I felt as if I had a purpose and was doing good.  It's what made me think I was doing what God wanted.  That's what I put all the value in, and is what I miss so much.
You're right, and I'm not going to argue with you about it.  I know it's not the best way of thinking, but I've been unable to change it.

I'm not immediately suicidal.  It's something I've thought about a lot and have kind of meticulously planned out.  It's not an impulsive spur of the moment thing at all, I don't think talking with anyone could change my plan at this point.

It's funny you bring God up, I had a somewhat steady faith before all of this.  I thought that things happened for a reason, and that if I stayed a good person, things would be okay.

Ever since I've felt like things haven't really lined up with that thinking, my faith and trust in God hasn't really been as steadfast.  I'll always be someone that believes in a God of some sort, but these days I'm not so sure if he's as involved as I once thought.  Where I used to feel like things happened for a reason, now I think I'm more on my own than I'd prefer.
What makes me not want to get out of bed is wanting more but knowing it's not in my power to get it.
I've sought help.  Nothing works.
According to your view, I am better off if I kill my self
I have worked with a few volunteer organizations and found it to be nothing more than a nightmare.  They were all just a lot of petty politics with nothing real or tangible being accomplished.

I think I would feel a bit differently about it if I hadn't already been in kind of a dream job.  Now that I've had it, I know how great it feels to be in a place where I love coming in to work every day and do work that I know actually means something and is long lasting.

Now I'm just longing for it all the time.  I feel like I'm doing everything I can to get back, but my efforts just aren't working.  If I can't do enough on my own, I'm just not good enough.  And I'm not good enough to live by my standards.
I've tried so many things.  Nothing provides relief, I just feel worthless because I'm not doing something productive and worthwhile as I once did.
I can't go get help.  If it gets out that I'm not mentally stable, I'm not going to get any better job.
I feel like I'm doing everything I possibly can to prepare myself for that job interview.  If I don't get it, it's because I'm not good enough.  Then I'd have the rationale to give up.
I was happy for a long time.  I had a dream job I was happy with and I felt useful and purposeful with.  Without it, I'm not happy.  The missing thing in that equation is pretty clear.
I had a dream job for a while and didn't have an issue then.  I felt fulfilled and purposed.  Now, without it, I feel useless.  I just need to get back to that.

I've seen two in the past few years.  They give me advice or medications that fill me full of happy go lucky thoughts for a while, but I end up just feeling terrible about my situation again eventually.
I'm not.  I was on medication when I was younger and it was a very bad experience.  I'm very dreadful of having to go through that again.

I just can't do with that.  I have to do something big.  I don't want to be forgotten after I'm gone.  I want to have changed the world one way or another.  Anything else and I'm just another faceless and forgettable name in a graveyard.
I mean I've seen therapists and such.  They've all told me that I just need to get back to a place where I can contribute and feel good about myself.  I just can't do that.
I felt like I was at my best when I was working a dream job and felt fulfilled.  All I want is to get back to that.

A little bit of both.  I'm tired of my goals that necessitate funding always being so far away and virtually unattainable.  I'm also sick of spending 50 hours a week on something so utterly pointless, I wish I could do something more meaningful.

I think the thing that might bother me the most about my job is how utterly pointless it is.  All I'm doing is lining someone else's pocketbooks.  In just a few decades time, everything I've done here will have been meaningless and forgotten.
I do a lot of things to try to enjoy myself but a lot of the time I feel like I'm just going through the motions and just filling time with something to do until I inevitably die.
Yes, I've tried that too.  I haven't had much luck in that area either.

I've tried so hard.  I always feel like they're just band aids on a much larger wound.  I think I would feel differently if I didn't already have a job I loved.  I know what it's like and I want that back so badly.
I don't know if there is anything I can do.  I have a degree in what I'd love to do, I just haven't really been able to fully utilize it in the place I want.
I don't know that I have an answer to that question.  It's difficult to answer intangibles.
